correctness.rationale: Given length r=2m−1 and n vertices, precisely n−1 labels are the unique forward edges E_{s,s+1}, leaving r−n+1 loop labels. If any vertex carries three loops, two label positions have the same odd/even parity. Exchanging these equal matrix units yields a distinct parity-preserving permutation with unchanged nonzero identity-order product, contradicting isolation. Hence at most two loops per vertex, r−n+1≤2n and 2m≤3n, or n≥ceil(2m/3). In Arhancet §7.1, v_k=1+floor(k/3), F_k=E_{v_{k−1},v_k}, k=1..2m−1 gives n=ceil(2m/3) and the proof establishes that the chosen Fourier coefficient/(1,n) entry has only identity parity-compatible ordering. Boundary n=1 and small m covered by the count; no claim about global minimal complete-contractivity level. The argument is exact, not dependent on truncated enumeration.
